newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Seagate raises China investment by $32 mln.
newsitem.headline: Seagate raises China investment by $32 mln.

text.p: Seagate Technology, the world's biggest independent disk drive maker, said on Friday it would double its investment in the Chinese city of Wuxi, bringing its total investment in China to US$90 million.

Seagate would spend an additional $32 million on building, renovation and equipment at its disk drive plant in Wuxi, said Richard Downing, senior vice president of Seagate Technology's Volume Manufacturing, Storage Products Group.
The investment, including an additional 58,000 sq ft building, would bring Seagate's fixed assets investment in Wuxi to $52 million and its total in China to $90 million, he said.
"We anticipate in June this year, we will be ready to move in," Downing told reporters. Production at the new building was expected to start in July, he added.
The Wuxi plant produced more than one million disk drives between July 1995 and March 1996 and the capacity was expected to double following the additional investment, Downing said.
He declined to give a breakdown of production capacities at Seagate's China plants.
Seagate stepped into China by setting up a disk drive plant in China's booming southern city of Shenzhen in 1992.

The Wuxi plant, built in July 1995, was the first to start operations at the Wuxi-Singapore Industrial Park, a $462-million venture between Wuxi Manucipal Government and a consortium led by the Singapore Technologies Industrial Corporation.
Seagate now produces 2.5 million disk drives in China each quarter.
